content: This information does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or suitable for your use. It is not intended to replace personalized medical advice and should not substitute for the guidance of your healthcare provider. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Uses: This medication is prescribed to treat a specific skin condition known as rosacea. It helps reduce the number of pimples and bumps on the face but may not significantly decrease redness. Although doxycycline belongs to the tetracycline class of antibiotics, it does not function as an antibiotic in this context because it does not inhibit bacterial growth. Do not use this product to treat infections, including viral infections like the common cold or flu. How to Use: Before starting this medication, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist, and review it again with each refill. Take this medication orally on an empty stomach, ideally at least one hour before or two hours after a meal, as directed by your doctor, usually once daily in the morning. Swallow the capsules whole without crushing or chewing them. Take the medication with a full glass of water (8 ounces or 240 milliliters) unless otherwise instructed. If stomach upset occurs, taking it with food or milk may help, but be aware that this may reduce the medication's effectiveness, especially if consumed with calcium-rich foods. Consult your doctor or pharmacist if you need to take it with food or milk. Avoid taking this medication within 2 to 3 hours of products containing aluminum, calcium, iron, magnesium, zinc, or bismuth subsalicylate, such as antacids, sucralfate, certain vitamins/minerals, dairy products, or calcium-enriched juices. For optimal results, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals and at the same time each day. Side Effects: Common side effects may include upset stomach, nausea, diarrhea, or mild headache. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. If IH develops, it typically resolves after stopping doxycycline, but there is a risk of permanent vision loss or blindness. This medication may also rarely cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridium difficile (C. diff), which can occur during or even weeks to months after treatment. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or new vaginal yeast infections. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. This is not a complete list of potential side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Precautions: Before taking doxycycline, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other tetracycline drugs (e.g., minocycline), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Doxycycline may interfere with live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine), reducing their effectiveness. Children under 8 years old may be more sensitive to side effects, particularly tooth discoloration, which has also been reported in older children and young adults. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as doxycycline can harm an unborn baby. Avoid becoming pregnant while using this medication. Doxycycline passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Doxycycline may interfere with certain lab tests, potentially causing false results. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Taking outdated tetracycline-related drugs can result in serious illness. Important Notes: This summary does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information tailored to your specific health needs.
